correctness.rationale: The quantified threshold, tomography, third-order witness, and Pareto asymptotic hold for the stated regenerative emitter. In G the reset is a self-loop; in E the next clock has rate gamma+sum(s_i)+r. A failed attempt adds a fresh min(U_i,Exp(r)) if shelved, otherwise zero, and restarts in G. The attempts give the displayed Laplace transform f(z)=p*gamma/H(z) and an exponential moment. For the cumulant step, the renewal MGF has time Laplace transform (1-f(z))/(z(1-exp(x)f(z))). The interarrival distribution has a density, hence |f(iu)|<1 for u!=0; f decays as O(|u|^-2) uniformly in a small strip by the displayed formula. Thus in a smaller strip for complex x near zero the only pole of the renewal MGF transform is the simple root H(z(x))=p*gamma*exp(x). Shifting the inversion contour (subtract 1/z first) gives an analytic nonzero leading residue and uniform exponentially smaller error; local Cauchy differentiation yields c_j=z^(j)(0). Three implicit derivatives give the reported ratios, including F-1=2p*gamma*(p*K-1)/H'(0)^2 and c3/c1=1-(p*gamma)^2*H'''(0)/H'(0)^3 at equality. H'''(0)>0. K strictly decreases to zero from half the weighted second moment (possibly infinite). Right continuity upgrades Laplace uniqueness to all t>0; decomposition into channels is not generally identifiable. After the Pareto rescaling v=rt, v^(1-alpha)*exp(-v) dominates, giving the exact amplitude by Gamma integration. The headline 'nonanalytic' should not be read as universal: for alpha=3/2, putting z=sqrt(r*tau) makes z*K(r) analytic and nonzero at z=0 by the erfc formula, so the threshold r(p) itself is analytic at zero by the implicit function theorem. The precise displayed power-law claim is correct. Fano equality concerns the limiting variance-to-mean ratio, not all second-order time correlations.
